title: Elongationless start-stop elements are stress-resilient translation gates that are more repressive than uTranslons.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the 72.8 MB Europe PMC supplement zip, unpacked the inner 68 MB Excel file, converted its 'Data' sheet to CSV (64 s) and parsed it. Verified: 19,514 unique Ensembl gene rows (rows 38-19551 of the sheet; rows 9-36 are a summary block and row 37 is the header); a 5' untranslated region (UTR) sequence for every gene (pure A/C/G/T, median 170 nt, 95th percentile 785, max 6,792, 150 exact duplicates); 286 measurement columns covering 30 perturbed translation factors from 48 source studies; the two side-by-side blocks share a gene-ID column that matches on all 19,514 rows; missing values coded as the string 'na'. Computed coverage per column (74 columns with >=15,000 values), cross-laboratory and within-study replicate correlations, simple-feature baselines, and the start-stop vs control group difference.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the transcript chosen per gene is the principal transcript with the longest 5' UTR from GENCODE v43 via the UCSC Table Browser; the biological interpretation of the repeat initiation/termination cycling mechanism; the reporter assay results (in the supplementary PDF, which I did not parse).

a1_downloadable.note: Opened it myself: no login, no application. Europe PMC supplementary zip (72.8 MB) -> inner zip -> 68 MB .xlsx. Nucleic Acids Research is fully open access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified in the file: 41 columns are already 'log2 fold change in translation efficiency' for a named factor depletion, plus 77 ribosome-footprint fold-change columns, 18 small-subunit occupancy columns, 11 RNA half-life and 10 RNA level columns. Nothing has to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: The actual 5' UTR nucleotide sequence is a column (UTR5_Seq) for all 19,514 genes, not an accession. Element sequence, position and 30-nt flanks are also given for start-stop and uTranslon genes.

a4_units_stated.note: Primary labels are log2 fold change, stated in the column name and in a 'Notes' sheet that defines all 15 data types. Trap recorded: the 11 RNA half-life columns are 'ppm transformed' with negative values where hours are claimed, so that block's units are not interpretable - avoid it.

a5_enough_rows.note: 19,514 genes; per-perturbation counts verified, e.g. eIF3D knockdown 17,157, eIF4A knockdown 15,127, DDX6 knockout 10,055, DENR knockout 6,165. 14,247 genes have >=20 of the 41 translation-efficiency columns.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 68 MB Excel file / 77 MB CSV; ~3 GB peak RAM
a6_fits_laptop.note: Whole table loads in pandas on a 16 GB laptop. Embedding 19,514 short sequences with a small nucleotide language model is CPU-feasible.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Exact match, verified by counting: 19,514 genes, 1,417 predicted start-stop, 708 core start-stop, 216 with a good Kozak context, 1,331 predicted uTranslon(u9), 621 core, 190 good Kozak, 463 control genes - every number in the Methods section.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are measured log2 fold changes from published ribosome profiling and RNA sequencing, not another model's output. One construction risk recorded: translation-efficiency fold change equals footprint fold change minus RNA fold change from the same experiment, so those sibling columns must never be used as features.

B1.why: One Excel sheet, one row per gene, unique Ensembl ID; the two side-by-side blocks matched on all 19,514 rows.

B2.why: Needed a custom parser: 5-row stacked header, 28 summary rows above the data, missing coded as 'na'.

B3.why: All log2 fold changes, but from 48 labs; I measured same-factor cross-lab Spearman of 0.01-0.48.

B4.why: No censored or qualitative values seen, but missingness is heavy: median 30 of 41 translation-efficiency columns present per gene.

B5.why: Zero duplicate gene rows; 150 duplicate 5' UTR sequences; several columns share identical names (average vs replicate).

B6.why: Notes sheet defines all 15 data types, abbreviations and 45 references; each column carries type/factor/source/comment. Five columns lack a source.

C1.why: Informative either way: either sequence predicts factor dependency, or we publish the measured noise ceiling that explains why not.

C2.why: Searched: models predict baseline translation efficiency (RiboNN, Optimus 5-Prime, UTR-LM) but none predicts response to factor depletion.

C3.why: Novel plus unique application: this 19,514 x 286 compiled matrix with sequences has never been used for machine learning.

C4.why: Each label column is one ribosome-profiling experiment with a knockdown: months of work and tens of thousands of dollars.

C5.why: I computed the dummy and simple-feature baselines myself: 5' UTR length gives Spearman up to 0.31.

D1.why: Open-weight DNA/RNA language models fit 5' UTR sequences directly: DNABERT-2, HyenaDNA, Nucleotide Transformer, RNA-FM, UTR-LM.

D2.why: 19,514 sequences, median 170 nt: embed once on CPU, cache, fit a ridge or small multi-task head.

D3.why: DNABERT-2 and HyenaDNA are Apache 2.0, RNA-FM is MIT; the paper's supplement is Nucleic Acids Research open access.

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes (chrom column present, verified) and cluster 5' UTRs by sequence identity.

E2.why: 24 chromosomes, 30 perturbed factors, 48 source studies - plenty of groups to hold out.

E3.why: Per-column mean is the dummy; I also computed a simple-feature baseline (length, GC, upstream AUG count).

E4.why: Measured it: within-study replicate Spearman 0.42 (ABCE1), 0.63 (ASCC3), 0.70 (eIF4A knockdown).

E5.why: Reproduced in the file: DENR knockout hits start-stop genes (median -0.213) vs control (+0.100), p=9.2e-18.

E6.why: Label shuffling and dinucleotide-shuffled sequences are trivially runnable on this table.

E7.why: Seven factors measured by two or three independent labs; 11 columns are mouse, giving a species transfer test.

E8.why: The paper's own genome-wide claim (start-stop more repressed than uTranslon) is recomputable from these exact columns.

G1.why: Verified present: Ensembl gene and transcript, Entrez, HGNC, OMIM, RefSeq, UniProt accession, GRCh38 and hg19 coordinates.

G2.why: gnomAD 5' UTR variants join on the hg19 5' UTR coordinate column; GTEx and Human Protein Atlas join on Ensembl gene.

G3.why: One gene = one chosen transcript, so gnomAD variants are one-to-many and variants in other isoforms' UTRs are lost.

G4.why: Asks whether 5' UTR positions under human population constraint are the ones that create initiation-factor dependency.

H1.why: All 19,514 genes present with both up and down changes, plus a purpose-built 463-gene length-matched control set.

H2.why: 48 studies and many labs, but almost all immortalised human cell lines; 11 mouse columns, no tissues.

H3.why: The honest claim is writable in one sentence and is bounded by the noise ceiling I measured.

H4.why: Sources are documented per column, but the near-zero cross-lab agreement is invisible unless you compute it.

I1.why: Translation-control labs (Teleman, Iwasaki, Gehring, Dikstein, this paper's group) and messenger RNA therapeutic UTR designers.

I2.why: Changes which reporter a lab builds, and whether anyone trusts a single knockdown dataset as truth.

I3.why: Spearman on held-out genes plus precision in the top 100 - exactly the shortlist a lab would test.

I4.why: Simple features already reach Spearman 0.31, so the complex part of the mapping may be small.

J1.why: Frozen language-model embeddings, multi-task heads, grouped splits, a measured noise ceiling: real modelling.

J2.why: Positive controls are named and checkable, but initiation-factor biology is specialised; a translation biologist would help.

J3.why: The parsed tidy table and the cross-lab reproducibility matrix are both shareable even if the model fails.

J4.why: Three weeks: one day parsing (mostly done), two days embeddings, the rest modelling and controls.

J5.why: Kill condition is concrete and pre-stated: no perturbation beaten by 0.05 Spearman over length alone in week one.

existing_models.name: RiboNN (Nature Biotechnology 2025, Sanofi) - a multi-task convolutional neural network predicting translation efficiency from messenger RNA sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported r=0.79 in human and r=0.78 in mouse for mean translation efficiency across cell types, trained on 3,819 ribosome-profiling datasets spanning 140+ cell types; split details not verified by me.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Per the paper summaries I read, cell-type-specific and condition-specific translation efficiency beyond the mean remains the hard part; responses to loss of a specific initiation factor are not modelled at all.

existing_models.name: Optimus 5-Prime (Sample et al. 2019) - a convolutional network predicting mean ribosome load from 5' untranslated region sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Explains up to 93% of mean ribosome load variance on a held-out random-UTR test set from a massively parallel reporter assay, and 81% on 38,789 truncated human UTRs.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation from synthetic random 5' UTRs to endogenous messenger RNAs in their native context.

existing_models.name: UTR-LM (Nature Machine Intelligence 2024) - a language model for 5' untranslated regions
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 1-6% higher Spearman than Optimus 5-Prime, FramePool and RNA-FM on mean ribosome load prediction from reporter-assay data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Decoding endogenous UTR function rather than reporter-library behaviour.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 or HyenaDNA (open-weight DNA language models), with UTR-LM as a domain-matched alternative and RiboNN embeddings as a comparison
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU: 19,514 sequences of median 170 nucleotides, embedded once and cached (~100 MB), then ridge or small multi-task head.
backbone.licence: DNABERT-2 Apache 2.0, HyenaDNA Apache 2.0, RNA-FM MIT - all permissive.

integration.partner_dataset: gnomAD v4 5' untranslated region variants (population allele frequencies), joined to GTEx tissue expression and the Human Protein Atlas
integration.join_key: hg19 5' UTR coordinates (column HG19_5UTRcoordinates, verified present) for gnomAD; Ensembl gene ID for GTEx and Human Protein Atlas
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Are the 5' untranslated region positions that human populations keep free of variation the same positions that make a messenger RNA depend on a particular translation initiation factor?

controls.positive_control: Two, both already checked in the file: DENR knockout reduces translation efficiency of start-stop genes (median -0.213) versus control genes (+0.100), Mann-Whitney p=9.2e-18; and the 5'TOP motif score tracks Torin1 (mTOR inhibitor) sensitivity in the expected direction (Spearman -0.177, n=3,720).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle each label column across genes and confirm collapse to zero correlation; refit on dinucleotide-shuffled 5' UTR sequences; train on 5' UTR length alone to measure the trivial component (Spearman up to 0.31, measured).
controls.external_validation: The same factor measured by independent labs: ABCE1 in three studies, eIF4A in three, ASCC3/DDX6/DENR/eIF4G2/eIF2D in two each; plus 11 mouse-derived columns for a species transfer test.

honest_claim_h3: From the 5' untranslated region sequence alone we can predict a modest but real fraction of the between-gene variation in how translation efficiency changes when a given initiation factor is depleted, as measured by one laboratory in an immortalised human cell line - and we can state how much of the unexplained variation is measurement noise rather than missing biology, because the same perturbations were measured by several labs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the beginning of a human messenger RNA to predict how much its protein output falls when a specific translation start-up protein is removed.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per human gene: the 5' untranslated region sequence (the stretch before the protein-coding part; median 170 letters), plus lengths, GC content and codon-usage numbers. 19,514 genes, verified by opening the file.
plain_idea.predict: The measured log2 fold change in translation efficiency when one of 30 translation factors is knocked down, knocked out or drug-inhibited. Truth comes from ribosome profiling (sequencing the messenger RNA fragments protected by ribosomes) in 48 published studies, already in the table as columns.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Translation-control labs could predict which factor an untested messenger RNA depends on before building a reporter, and messenger RNA therapeutic designers could choose 5' untranslated regions that keep working under stress. Even if the model fails, the cross-laboratory reproducibility matrix tells the field which published knockdown datasets agree with each other.

more_or_better_data.why: RiboNN was trained on 3,819 ribosome-profiling datasets but on baseline translation efficiency only; none of RiboNN, Optimus 5-Prime or UTR-LM covers response to loss of a named initiation factor. This table has 286 measurement columns over 30 perturbed factors, with up to 17,157 genes per column.

confidence_score.why: Replicate columns within studies and two or three independent labs for seven factors let us attach a measured noise ceiling to each prediction (within-study replicate Spearman 0.42-0.70, cross-lab 0.01-0.48). I did not verify whether RiboNN reports calibrated uncertainty, so I cannot claim this is unique.

models_beatable.why: For the exact task there is nothing to beat. For the adjacent baseline-translation-efficiency task, RiboNN is a 2025 Nature Biotechnology model with open code and strong numbers, so we should use it as a feature source or baseline rather than try to beat it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Extra ribosome-profiling knockdowns from GEO would come from different labs, and I measured near-zero cross-lab agreement for the same factor (ABCE1 Spearman 0.01-0.19, eIF2D -0.03, eIF4G2 0.05), so adding them could add noise rather than signal. The 'same quantity measured the same way' condition fails.

label_elsewhere.sources: GEO holds hundreds of ribosome-profiling knockdown and knockout experiments, and the RiboNN atlas (3,819 ribosome-profiling datasets, 140+ cell types, Nature Biotechnology 2025, code at github.com/Sanofi-Public/RiboNN) covers baseline translation efficiency. Massively parallel reporter data from Optimus 5-Prime gives 5' UTR to mean ribosome load for roughly 280,000 random and 30,000 human UTRs. All found by search; I did not download them.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Ensembl gene ID (and hg19/GRCh38 coordinates for reporter-assay UTRs)
label_elsewhere.why: Baseline translation efficiency is abundantly measured elsewhere and gives an external check on the sequence features, but the specific label here - the change on depleting one named factor - would have to be reprocessed from raw GEO submissions, so there is no ready-made joinable resource.

risks: Paralogous or near-identical 5' untranslated regions split across training and test: I found 150 exactly duplicated UTR sequences among 19,514 genes.
Translation-efficiency fold change equals ribosome-footprint fold change minus RNA fold change from the same experiment, so using those sibling columns as features is leakage by construction.
Which genes have a value in a column depends on sequencing depth, which correlates with gene expression and with 5' UTR length, so missingness is informative.
The start-stop and uTranslon class columns are computable from the 5' UTR sequence itself, so predicting them from sequence would be circular.
Eleven columns are mouse measurements mapped onto human genes by orthology, mixing species if used as held-out tests of a human-sequence model.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes using the 'chrom' column (verified present in the file), and additionally cluster 5' UTRs at 80% sequence identity with CD-HIT-EST and hold out clusters. For transfer, leave-one-source-study-out using the source row of the header (48 studies).
checks: Shuffle each label column across genes and confirm Spearman collapses to zero.
Train on 5' UTR length alone and report it as the trivial component (measured: up to Spearman 0.31 against DAP5/eIF4G2 knockout).
Report the nearest-neighbour 5' UTR sequence identity between each test gene and the training set.
Check whether missingness per column predicts the label, by fitting on the missingness pattern alone.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: the chromosome column is present, sequence clustering is one CD-HIT run, and the only subtle trap (sibling footprint/RNA columns) is avoidable by using sequence features only.

success_criteria.metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and measured log2 translation-efficiency fold change on held-out chromosomes, computed per perturbation, plus precision among the top 100 predicted most factor-dependent genes - the shortlist a lab would actually test with reporters.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-column mean gives Spearman 0 by construction. Simple-feature baselines I measured in the file: 5' UTR length vs DAP5/eIF4G2 knockout translation efficiency -0.314 (n=9,084), vs Torin1 +0.310 (n=4,147); GC content vs DDX6 knockout -0.266 (n=10,055). No published model exists for this task.
success_criteria.success: Beat the simple-feature ridge by at least 0.08 Spearman on at least 10 of the roughly 20 well-covered perturbations on held-out chromosomes, while recovering both positive controls (DENR/start-stop, 5'TOP/Torin1).
success_criteria.noise_ceiling: Measured within-study replicate Spearman: eIF4A knockdown 0.70, ASCC3 knockdown 0.63, ABCE1 knockdown 0.42. Cross-laboratory agreement for the same factor ranges 0.01-0.48, so for several factors the ceiling is effectively zero.
success_criteria.kill: If after one week no perturbation is predicted better than 5' UTR length alone by at least 0.05 Spearman on held-out chromosomes, stop and publish only the reproducibility matrix.

ambitious.why: Publishes sequence-to-function models with genome-wide reanalysis; would need the model to transfer across independent labs and to reveal interpretable 5' untranslated region determinants of factor dependency.

realistic.why: Publishes focused benchmarks and reanalyses of published genomics data; the likely result - language-model embeddings modestly beating simple features on about half the perturbations, bounded by a measured noise ceiling - fits exactly.

fallback.why: Even if no model works, the parsed and documented 19,514-gene by 286-measurement table with sequences, plus the cross-laboratory reproducibility matrix, is a reusable resource with a clear provenance trail.

pitch.headline: 19,514 human 5' untranslated region sequences in one table alongside 286 measured translation responses to 30 different translation factors being removed.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Verified by opening the file: sequences and labels in the same sheet, 48 source studies, seven factors measured by two or three independent labs, and a purpose-built 463-gene length-matched control set.
pitch.the_win: Beat 5' UTR length alone (Spearman 0.31 against DAP5/eIF4G2 knockout, measured) by 0.08 or more on ten perturbations, approaching the 0.63-0.70 within-study replicate ceiling.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We publish the first cross-laboratory reproducibility matrix for translation-factor knockdown datasets - I already measured ABCE1 agreeing at Spearman 0.01 between two labs, which the field reuses as truth.
pitch.who_wants_it: Translation-control labs (Teleman, Iwasaki, Gehring, Dikstein, this paper's group) deciding which reporter to build, and messenger RNA therapeutic designers choosing stress-resilient 5' untranslated regions.

ml_idea: Multi-task regression from human 5' untranslated region sequence to the measured log2 change in translation efficiency across roughly 20 well-covered translation-factor depletions. Freeze an open-weight DNA language model (DNABERT-2 or HyenaDNA), cache embeddings for all 19,514 sequences once on CPU, and fit a shared trunk with one head per perturbation, masking missing labels. Evaluate per perturbation on held-out chromosomes and sequence-identity clusters, against a simple-feature ridge and the measured replicate noise ceiling, with leave-one-lab-out transfer as the headline generalisation test.

effort.compute_note: I timed the Excel-to-CSV conversion at 64 seconds and the full-table pandas scans at a few seconds each on this laptop; embedding time is an estimate from typical CPU throughput of a small nucleotide language model on 19,514 sequences of median 170 nucleotides, and the cross-validation estimate assumes a ridge head on cached embeddings.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: For every factor measured by two independent labs, correlate the two columns. I already ran it: ABCE1 0.01-0.19, eIF2D -0.03, eIF4G2 0.05, DENR 0.25, DDX6 0.48. So restrict the project up front to perturbations whose within-study replicate Spearman is at least 0.5 (eIF4A 0.70, ASCC3 0.63 qualify).

verdict_reason: Part A passes on files I opened: 19,514 genes with their 5' untranslated region sequences and 286 already-measured log2 fold-change columns over 30 translation factors, counts matching the paper exactly, parsed on a laptop, with a positive control reproduced (DENR knockout hits start-stop genes, p=9.2e-18). The one thing to verify before committing is label quality per perturbation: I measured near-zero cross-laboratory agreement for ABCE1, eIF2D and eIF4G2, and simple sequence features already reach Spearman 0.31, so spend the first day selecting the subset of perturbations whose within-study replicate correlation exceeds 0.5 and confirming a language-model head beats length alone there.
